mechanics.name: Urban Evasion
mechanics.currentEffect: Permanently increases your Movement speed while crouched by 90/95/100%.
activation: Ends/deactivates when: The bonus applies only while crouched.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (1.7.0): Removed the uninjured requirement and increased crouched movement speed bonus to 90/95/100%.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: Lets you move faster while crouching.

editorial.summary: Move at normal walking speed while crouched at Tier III.
useCases: Reposition around low cover without standing and exposing your model.
Move quickly while avoiding some Killer sightlines and powers that care about posture.
Navigate stealth-heavy indoor or edge-map situations with less crouch-speed penalty.
counters: Crouching is still slower than running.
Overusing the perk can destroy map tempo.
Many Killers can detect or pressure crouched Survivors normally.
pros: Removes the normal movement tax from crouching relative to walking.
Useful around low obstacles and stealth situations.
cons: Easy to misuse by crouching unnecessarily.
No chase burst or action-speed benefit.
Often weaker than simply learning when to run.
analysis: Urban Evasion ranks this position because moving at walking speed while crouched is useful in specific geometry, but the perk has an infamous trap: it can make inefficient movement feel safe. The effect is strongest when crouching is already the correct tactical choice.
Low-cover tiles and certain Killer interactions can reward staying crouched while repositioning. In those moments, doubling crouch movement speed makes the posture much less costly.

The problem is players treating crouching as a default travel mode. Even fast crouching is dramatically slower than sprinting across the map, and map pressure is often more important than avoiding a hypothetical detection event.
Urban Evasion is therefore a decent utility perk with a behavior tax. Used deliberately it has a niche; used constantly it can make the player less effective than if they had equipped nothing.
editorial.verdict: A situational movement tool, not permission to crouch everywhere. Urban Evasion is good when posture matters and bad when it replaces normal rotation speed.
